name: xcodegen
description: Generate your Xcode project from a spec file and your folder structure

repo.name: XcodeGen
repo.description: A Swift command line tool for generating your Xcode project

readme.summary: Excellent clarity and installation coverage with a solid quick-start example, but lacks any troubleshooting guidance.
readme.top_issue: No troubleshooting section — common problems like spec errors, missing Xcode version, or build setting conflicts are not addressed.

common_complaints: Frequent regressions in recent versions (2.44.x, 2.45.x) breaking core functionality
Path handling bugs causing build failures (absolute paths, folder sources, synced folders)
Xcode version compatibility issues and object version mismatches
Silent failures (includes silently ignored, null entries not validated)
Performance degradation (4.5GB memory usage from null source entries)
sentiment.summary: Community health is concerning due to quality control issues with breaking regressions in consecutive releases, though issues are being closed indicating active maintenance rather than abandonment.

red_flags: Some responses are brief and could be more detailed for complex issues
Closing a pull request due to maintenance burden without alternative solutions
communication.summary: The maintainer provides helpful and clear guidance, with some technical depth, but could improve patience in handling repeated questions and welcomingness by offering more support or alternatives.

concerns: 376 open issues with zero resolution in past 6 months
No merged PRs or closed issues in past 6 months despite recent commit
Zero active contributors in past 6 months
Unknown or missing last release information
Large issue backlog suggests maintainer not triaging/responding
positive_signals: Recent commit 3 days ago indicates project is not completely abandoned
maintenance.summary: Project receives occasional commits but shows no community engagement or active maintenance, with 376 unresolved issues suggesting the maintainer is not actively managing the project.

changelog.summary: The changelog is well-organized and clearly marks breaking changes, but lacks migration guides.

governance.summary: The governance documentation for XcodeGen outlines a clear path for contributions but lacks details on succession planning, decision-making processes, and indicates a single maintainer with merge rights.
